passages.original: Bel• lum Lihi, inquit, indicitur, in quo cnitescas pugnando, ut ad plenam pacem triumphando pervenias. Non contra unum dimicabis; multi cnim contra te exient adversarii : pugnabis enim cum vitiis, et. ut beatus martyr Cyprianus ait, si depresseris avaritiam, exsurget libido; quod et si libidinem superabis, succedet ambitio ; et si amhitio a te fuerit devicta, ira, zelus, amulatio, invidentia, superbia, ebriositas cum cæteris suis pestiferis sociis in unum contra le dimicantium constituent castra (Cyp.
passages.english: "A war," he says, "is declared on you, in which you are to shine by fighting, so that by triumphing you may come to full peace." You will not fight against one [enemy]; for many adversaries will come out against you. For you will fight with vices, and, as the blessed martyr Cyprian says, if you have beaten down avarice, lust will rise up; and if you overcome lust, ambition will follow; and if ambition has been conquered by you, anger, jealousy, rivalry, envy, pride, drunkenness, with the rest of their pestilent allies, will pitch together the camp of those fighting against you (Cyprian,

The speaker of 'inquit' is not identified in the passage; presumably the King (Christ) mentioned in the preceding context.
